results.reply:
I am Haq. I understand your frustration, but as a legal-help assistant, I must stick to the verified laws that actually help you get your money back. Filing a criminal case for salary non-payment is rarely the right path; the Code on Wages, 2019, is specifically designed to handle this quickly and effectively. Let's focus on the law that works.

**Your legal position:**
You have a clear path to recover your dues under the Code on Wages, 2019. This law covers all employees, regardless of salary, and provides a specific authority to hear your claim. Your case is strongest when you have proof of employment and a clear record of the unpaid period.

**Law you can cite:**
* Code on Wages, 2019, Section 17: Wages must be paid by the 7th of the next month; this is your statutory right.
* Code on Wages, 2019, Section 45: You can file a claim for unpaid wages with the government-appointed authority within 3 years.
* Code on Wages, 2019, Section 51: The Inspector-cum-Facilitator can assist you in filing your claim.

**What to do now:**
1. Send a formal email to your employer listing the exact months and amount due; keep a copy.
2. If they do not pay, send a formal demand notice (I can help you draft this).
3. File your claim on the SAMADHAN portal (https://samadhan.labour.gov.in).
4. Call 15100 (NALSA) for free legal aid if you need further guidance.

**I need from you:**
1. What is the name of your company?
2. Do you have an offer letter or payslips as proof of employment?

_⚠️ I removed a legal reference I could not verify. Please confirm the exact law with a lawyer or free legal aid (NALSA helpline 15100)._

citations.title: Deadline for paying wages, including after leaving the job
citations.plain: Wages are due by these deadlines: daily workers at the end of the shift; weekly workers on the last working day of the week; fortnightly workers before the end of the second day after the fortnight; monthly workers before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If you are removed, dismissed, retrenched or resign, or lose your job because the establishment closes, your wages must be paid within two working days.

citations.title: Filing a wage claim: who decides it and the 3-year limit
citations.plain: Wage claims under the Code are heard by an authority the Government appoints, who must be at least a Gazetted Officer. The claim can be filed by you, your registered trade union, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator. File within 3 years of the date the claim arises; a later claim may still be accepted if you show sufficient cause. Besides the amount due, the authority can award compensation of up to ten times the claim, and it tries to decide within three months.

citations.title: Inspector-cum-Facilitators
citations.plain: The Code replaces the old 'Inspector' with an 'Inspector-cum-Facilitator', appointed by the Government. This officer advises employers and workers on compliance, inspects establishments, and can file a wage claim on a worker's behalf under section 45.

citations.title: SAMADHAN: online portal for labour disputes and claims (central sphere)
citations.plain: SAMADHAN (https://samadhan.labour.gov.in) is the labour ministry's online portal for raising industrial disputes and, since its 2.0 upgrade, filing claims under the Labour Codes and tracking them. It is run by the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) machinery, so it mainly serves establishments where the Central Government is the appropriate Government. For most private employers, the state labour department is the forum.

citations.title: NALSA legal aid helpline 15100
citations.plain: Call the national legal aid helpline 15100 (toll-free) for free legal advice and help applying for legal aid. You can also apply for legal aid or victim compensation online via the NALSA website.
